howDoI.q: How do I make a monster go away by itself after a while?
How do I leave a sparkle where a monster was?
How do I make a monster that Mia cannot walk through?
How do I make one monster turn into another after a while?
How do I make a monster stop blocking the way when it changes?
How do I make the new monster walk about?

pages.head: Welcome
pages.html:
Welcome

Here Today is a Starter: a small game that shows a few Game-Maker ideas, with signs in the levels that say what you are looking at. It has two short levels and takes a couple of minutes to finish.

Play it first. Then open it in Game-Maker (Edit a copy on the home page keeps the original safe) and read the pages below, which say where each thing in the levels is made.

The keys

Left and Right walk. Space jumps. F2 shows your lives, hit points and score. Walk into the door at the end of a level to go on.

Some monsters have a lifetime: a number of ticks (about 18 a second). When it is up, the monster is gone, or it becomes another monster. Nothing in this game hurts you.

pages.head: Level 1: A Bubble
pages.html:
Level 1: A Bubble

The THIS BUBBLE POPS ON ITS OWN sign stands in front of a brick wall with a low tunnel through it, and a clear bubble sits in the tunnel. Walk into it and Mia stops: the bubble is solid. It does not hurt, it just does not move.

The WAIT FOR IT TO GO sign says what to do. After about twenty seconds from the start of the level, the bubble pops into a sparkle and the way is clear. Walk through.

There are six coins on the way, worth ten points each.

pages.head: How this level is made
pages.html:
How level 1 is made

  • A lifetime. Open here.mon in the monsters editor and pick the bubble. Under Lives it says For a set time, and the Lifetime (ticks) is 340: about eighteen and a half seconds at 18.2 ticks a second. When the time is up, the bubble is destroyed on its own, with no help from Mia.
  • The clock. A monster is born when its scene starts, so the lifetime counts from the start of the level, not from the moment Mia gets there. Mia arrives after about ten seconds, so she waits about eight. Slow readers find the bubble already gone, which is fine: the way is just open.
  • The sparkle. The bubble's When destroyed it becomes is the sparkle, a short-lived monster of its own, so the pop leaves a twinkle for half a second and then that is gone too.
  • Monsters that block. Monsters are not solid unless their picture is. Open here.mbl in the blocks editor: the Solid boxes of bubble0 and bubble1 are checked on every side, which holds the hero back, and they take no hit points. The bubble's power is 110, because a monster under 100 is also destroyed when the hero touches it.
  • The tunnel. Open one.map in the map editor. It is two blocks high, the hero's own height, cut through a wall of brick that goes up to the top of the room, so there is no way over the bubble.
  • The signs. Each sign is a few ordinary blocks side by side, with the words drawn in their pictures.

pages.head: Level 2: Wake Up
pages.html:
Level 2: Wake Up

The A SLEEPY ONE BLOCKS THE TUNNEL sign points at a blue gumdrop with closed eyes and a little z, sitting in a tunnel. It is solid, just like the bubble.

The LATER IT BECOMES AN AWAKE ONE sign says what happens. This time the monster does not vanish. After about eighteen seconds it wakes up and becomes a different monster: orange, eyes open, and not solid. It strolls back and forth a few blocks, and Mia can walk right through it.

There are six coins, two before the tunnel and four after it.

pages.head: How this level is made
pages.html:
How level 2 is made

  • Becomes another. Open here.mon and pick the sleeper. It lives For a set time (340 ticks), and its When destroyed it becomes is the awake one instead of nothing. When the lifetime is up, the game puts the awake one in the same place and starts it afresh.
  • A new start. The awake one has its own picture, its own solid setting, its own path and its own lifetime. The sleeper's solid picture is swapped for a picture that is not solid, which is why the tunnel opens.
  • Stays. The awake one's Lives is Forever (indestructible), so it keeps strolling.
  • The stroll. Its Movement path is three blocks to the right and back at a slow speed. It starts from where the sleeper was.
  • One clock. Everything put on a map starts its clock when the level starts. A chain of monsters, one becoming the next, can run a whole little story that way, with no help from the hero.
  • The exit. The last door links to the The End scene in here.gam, which plays the ending.

pages.head: What Game-Maker cannot do
pages.html:
What Game-Maker cannot do

A lifetime is a plain timer, and that is all it is:

  • The clock cannot start on a trigger. A monster's lifetime starts when the monster is born, and monsters put on the map are born when the level starts. Mia arriving or touching something starts nothing. To start a timer later, give birth to the monster later, for example from a block.
  • Going out through a door and back into the same scene starts the level again, and every clock with it.
  • The time is a number of ticks, at most 32,767 (about half an hour). It is the same every time, with no randomness.
  • A monster that becomes another cannot pass anything along: the new one starts from its own settings, with its own picture, path and lifetime.

pages.head: Make it yours
pages.html:
Make it yours

Try one change at a time, and play after each:

  • Change the bubble's Lifetime (ticks) to 120. It pops before Mia gets there. Try 900, and Mia waits a long while.
  • Change what the bubble becomes to the awake one. Now the bubble turns into an orange gumdrop where it pops.
  • Make the awake one Lives For a set time too, and have it become the sleeper. They take turns forever.
  • Put a second sleeper a little further into the tunnel with a longer lifetime.
  • Make the awake one solid in the blocks editor, and see the way stay blocked.

The home page's Starters tab has more small games like this one.
